verifications.verifierNote: Fixture and mechanism confirmed; the headline claim overshoots and the finding duplicates F029's test observation. VERIFIED: errors.test.ts:4-6 `function apiError(status: number, message = 'boom') { return Object.assign(new Error(message), { name: 'ApiError', status }); }`; the it.each table at lines 14-23 with `[403, 'invalid-key']` at line 17 and the assertion at line 22. VERIFIED precedence in errors.ts:53-61 — `lower.includes('quota')` at 53, then `lower.includes('safety') || lower.includes('blocked')` at 54, and only in the trailing `else` at 57-61 does `statusOf(error)` run. So 'boom' (which contains none of those substrings and is neither a SyntaxError nor a TypeError) does fall through to the status switch — the discoverer's mechanism is right. REFUTED SUB-CLAIM: 'the 403 -> invalid-key assertion proves nothing.' It proves the status branch maps correctly for a message with no trigger substring, which is a real (if narrow) unit. More importantly, errors.test.ts:25-27 ('detects a quota message ahead of the raw status', asserting `apiError(429, 'Quota exceeded...')` -> 'quota') and errors.test.ts:29-31 ('maps a safety block', asserting `apiError(400, 'Response blocked due to SAFETY')` -> 'safety') show the message-before-status precedence is deliberate and explicitly covered — it is not something the 'boom' fixture is concealing. WHAT SURVIVES, and is real: no test in the file ever passes a realistic SDK message. Per node_modules/@google/genai/dist/web/index.mjs:14249-14254 the SDK sets `message` to `JSON.stringify(errorBody)` — the entire error document — so any 4xx whose body contains the substring 'blocked' or 'quota' anywhere (field names and nested details included) is misclassified, and this fixture models ApiError's SHAPE but not its CONTENT, so the suite cannot detect it. NOT REPO-VERIFIABLE: the specific wording 'Requests from referer <empty> are blocked.' is external knowledge; I could not confirm it from this repo, only the mechanism. Amended to medium: this is the test-side sibling of F029 (which I confirmed at high), and its own headline is overstated.
verifications.reachability: The test defect itself is not user-reachable. The production misclassification it fails to catch is F029's: any Gemini 4xx whose JSON body contains 'blocked' or 'quota' is tagged 'safety'/'quota' before errors.ts:58-61 ever reads the typed `status`.

What the fixture does hide is that it models ApiError's shape but never its content: per node_modules/@google/genai/dist/web/index.mjs:14249-14254 the SDK's `message` is `JSON.stringify(errorBody)` — the whole error document — so any 4xx body containing 'blocked' or 'quota' anywhere is misclassified before the typed `status` is read, and no test in this file would notice. verifications.verifierNote: Pattern and runtime behaviour CONFIRMED by execution; severity amended down because the finding's own honest reachability note is correct and I re-verified it. Pattern at errors.ts:39-42 verbatim: `function statusOf(error: unknown): number | undefined { const status = (error as { status?: unknown }).status; ... }`. I reproduced the behaviour in node with the identical property read: null -> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'status')`; undefined -> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'status')`; 'str' -> undefined; 42 -> undefined; true -> undefined; {status:429} -> 429. The internal inconsistency is real: errors.ts:48 `error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)` explicitly anticipates non-Error input, and then line 40 dereferences the same value unguarded — and line 40 is only reached via the `else` at line 57, i.e. after the string branches have already run on a `String(null)` = 'null'. Blast radius CONFIRMED exactly as claimed by grep: 16 direct `toAiError(` call sites outside errors.ts — 9 in src/lib/ai (client.ts:26, chat.ts:18, chat.ts:37, quiz.ts:19, recommend.ts:41, summarize.ts:56, summarize.ts:77, summarize.ts:101, tts.ts:32) and 7 in UI (AppShell.tsx:48, ChatModal.tsx:72, BookDetail.tsx:169, BookDetail.tsx:189, EReader.tsx:213, QuizModal.tsx:65, ApiKeyDialog.tsx:33), plus 3 indirect via handleAiError (AppShell.tsx:47-56 -> LibraryPage.tsx:80, LibraryPage.tsx:98, AddBookModal via AppShell.tsx:196). REACHABILITY re-verified independently: `grep -rn 'throw |Promise.reject' src/` excluding `throw new ` returns only the 9 `throw toAiError(error)` lines — every other throw in src/ is `throw new <Error subclass>`, and there is no bare `Promise.reject()`. So no in-repo producer can trigger this today; the exposure is entirely third-party (the SDK, fetch, a future dependency). SDK check: node_modules/@google/genai/dist/web/index.mjs:14251 and :13971 both throw `new ApiError({...})`, which is an Error. Under the spec's scale, a latent defect with a trivial fix and no current in-repo trigger is medium ('erodes confidence and refactor safety'), not high.
